claim_boundary: This catalog records discovered sources and interface facts. V4 automatic selection is determined separately by access status, research-use status, evidence tier, use mode, frozen spatial/geology compatibility, and execution context; legacy production_eligible is compatibility-only. Catalog inclusion is not scientific endorsement.

georoc-archaean.title: GEOROC Compilation: Archaean Cratons

coverage.notes: Global distribution of Archaean cratons only; not representative of all rock geochemistry.

license.notes: Retain GEOROC and original publication citations.

limitations: Precompiled selected values are not an unfiltered set of every replicate determination.

georoc-antarctica-intraplate.title: GEOROC Compilation: Intraplate Volcanic Rocks — Antarctica member

coverage.notes: 424 literature-linked whole-rock rows; a discrete compilation, not uniform Antarctica coverage.

license.notes: Retain GEOROC and original-publication citations.

limitations: The compilation follows published sampling and is spatially uneven.
One coordinate range is not an exact point and is not converted to a midpoint.
The winning row-level analytical method is absent from the precompiled member.
This member shares the GEOROC compilation lineage and is not an independent rock-source family.

usgs-conus-soil.title: Geochemical and mineralogical data for soils of the conterminous United States

coverage.notes: Three sampled soil layers in CONUS; not global soil coverage.

license.notes: USGS-produced data are public domain; credit and dataset citation are retained.

limitations: Soil layers and legacy qualifier encodings must remain distinct.

georoc-database.title: GEOROC Database

coverage.notes: Published igneous and metamorphic rocks, glasses, minerals and inclusions; coverage follows available literature.

license.notes: Database query data require GEOROC and original source citation; repository datasets may have separate terms.

limitations: Only a test API endpoint has been documented in this discovery round; production endpoint and response version must be verified.
Aggregated records must retain every original publication reference.

usgs-ngdb.title: U.S. Geological Survey National Geochemical Database

coverage.notes: Primarily inorganic elemental concentrations for US and Alaska geologic samples.

license.notes: Individual releases and non-USGS contributions still require dataset-level review.

limitations: Historical databases contain heterogeneous methods, qualifiers and reporting units.
A specific immutable data release must be selected before production use.

gemstat-open-archive.title: UNEP GEMS/Water Global Freshwater Quality Archive v3 seven-element subset
gemstat-open-archive.publisher: UNEP GEMS/Water Programme, GEMS/Water Data Centre and German Federal Institute of Hydrology

coverage.notes: The audited As/Cr/Cu/Hg/Ni/Pb/Zn subset contains 3,739,180 target observations representing 689,291 station-date-time-depth sampling events at 17,248 stations in 35 countries. River, lake, groundwater, reservoir and wetland coverage is spatially and temporally uneven.

license.notes: The v3 Zenodo record and included README identify CC BY 4.0; retain archive citation and record DOI.

limitations: The seven-element subset covers 35 voluntarily contributing countries and is not a uniform global freshwater grid.
Dissolved, extractable, suspended and total operational fractions must remain separate; Cr-VI is excluded from elemental chromium.
Only 279,225 of 3,739,180 target observations have a defined analysis method, so method-comparable subsets are substantially smaller.
The source contains 1,836,306 censored values plus Pending review and Suspect rows that remain traceable and must be filtered according to use.
Rows for different elements or fractions at the same station, date, time and depth are one physical sampling event, not independent evidence.
The v3 description claims 22,982 stations and 622 parameters, while the selected metadata files contain 22,981 rows and 621 parameters.
Eleven required ZIP members were locally range-verified by DOI/version, byte ranges, member names, decoded sizes, schema and row counts; the complete 201 MB archive was not downloaded locally.

wosis.title: World Soil Information Service (WoSIS)

coverage.notes: Quality-assessed and standardised soil profile data shared by many providers; coverage and property availability vary.

license.notes: Public records can include CC BY and CC BY-NC; license must be retained and filtered at record level.

limitations: WoSIS contains standardised soil properties, not a single uniform total-element geochemistry program.
Dynamic WFS and immutable DOI snapshot are separate acquisition modes.
Non-commercial license records are not eligible under open-only production policy.

earthchem-portal.title: EarthChem Portal

coverage.notes: Federated discovery across participating solid-earth geochemistry databases.

license.notes: Retain the original database, dataset and publication terms for every record.

limitations: Aggregator results are discovery leads, not independent corroborating sources.
Production records must resolve to an upstream database or DOI dataset.

gemas-europe.title: Geochemical Mapping of Agricultural and Grazing Land Soil (GEMAS)
gemas-europe.publisher: Geological Survey Ireland distribution of the EuroGeoSurveys GEMAS project

coverage.notes: Harmonised agricultural and grazing land soil survey for Europe.

license.notes: GSI catalogue terms are CC BY 4.0; retain GSI distribution and upstream GEMAS attribution.

limitations: The 4,131 valid samples are a low-density European survey, not continuous coverage.
Modified aqua-regia and XRF results are separate measurement bases.
XRF half-detection-limit substitutions cannot recover original censor qualifiers.
GSI distribution is not an independent field-sampling lineage from GEMAS.

petdb.title: PetDB EarthChem Data Synthesis

coverage.notes: Published igneous and metamorphic rock, glass, inclusion and mineral chemistry, concentrated on ocean-floor and mantle settings.

license.notes: Site license is CC BY-SA 4.0; every record must also retain its original publication and contributing-dataset citation.

limitations: Dynamic holdings require a query timestamp, exported record inventory and upstream-reference deduplication.
Database aggregation is not independent corroboration of GEOROC or original publications.

foregs-europe.title: FOREGS-EuroGeoSurveys Geochemical Atlas of Europe baseline data
foregs-europe.publisher: EuroGeoSurveys and Geological Survey of Finland

coverage.notes: Harmonised low-density European baseline survey of topsoil, subsoil, humus, stream/floodplain sediment and stream water.

license.notes: Pages state that the database is freely downloadable and prescribe atlas citation/copyright; machine-readable redistribution terms still need legal review.

limitations: Very low continental sampling density is not local coverage.
Multiple techniques and laboratories must remain explicit even though sampling was harmonised.

foregs-topsoil.title: FOREGS Geochemical Atlas of Europe: topsoil
foregs-topsoil.publisher: EuroGeoSurveys and Geological Survey of Finland

coverage.notes: Low-density harmonised FOREGS residual topsoil, 0-25 cm without organic layer observations; not continuous or local coverage.

interfaces.access: free_download_citation_terms; archive HTTP transport restricted to exact official URL with redirects rejected

license.notes: Research use with Salminen et al. (2005) citation and the published EuroGeoSurveys/GTK copyright notice; no broad redistribution license is inferred.

limitations: About one sample per 4,700 square kilometres; continental baseline does not imply local coverage.
Measurement bases and methods remain explicit and are not silently pooled.
Published numeric CSVs do not preserve row-level less-than qualifiers; half-DL values are treated as possible upstream substitutions.
The publisher archive endpoint currently uses legacy HTTP; the adapter rejects redirects and validates byte count, member inventory, schema and row counts.

foregs-subsoil.publisher: EuroGeoSurveys and Geological Survey of Finland

foregs-floodplain-sediment.title: FOREGS Geochemical Atlas of Europe: floodplain sediment
foregs-floodplain-sediment.publisher: EuroGeoSurveys and Geological Survey of Finland

coverage.notes: Low-density harmonised FOREGS floodplain sediment from a larger drainage basin observations; not continuous or local coverage.

interfaces.access: free_download_citation_terms; archive HTTP transport restricted to exact official URL with redirects rejected

license.notes: Research use with Salminen et al. (2005) citation and the published EuroGeoSurveys/GTK copyright notice; no broad redistribution license is inferred.

limitations: About one sample per 4,700 square kilometres; continental baseline does not imply local coverage.

canada-cdogs.title: Canadian Database of Geochemical Surveys (CDoGS)
canada-cdogs.publisher: Natural Resources Canada, Geological Survey of Canada

coverage.notes: Catalogue of more than 1,300 Canadian regional geochemical surveys; standardized raw downloads are available for a subset.

license.notes: Federal and provincial releases can use different Open Government licences; pin and retain the licence of each selected release.

limitations: Only a subset of catalogued surveys currently has standardized raw downloads.
Reanalysis and republication histories can create related records that must not be counted as independent samples.

australia-ngsa.title: National Geochemical Survey of Australia
australia-ngsa.publisher: Geoscience Australia and Australian state/territory geological surveys

coverage.notes: Ultra-low-density catchment-outlet transported regolith survey covering more than 90 percent of Australia; useful nationally, not locally.

license.notes: Geoscience Australia material is generally CC BY 4.0, but each selected data product must be checked for third-party exceptions.

limitations: Catchment-outlet transported regolith is not interchangeable with in-situ topsoil or stream sediment.
The sampling density is designed for national-scale patterns, not site-scale prediction.

australia-ozchem.title: OZCHEM National Whole Rock and Stream Sediment Geochemistry Database

coverage.notes: National compilation of located whole-rock and stream-sediment analyses from Geoscience Australia and other surveys.

license.notes: Current product-specific licensing and any contributed state data exceptions need confirmation.

limitations: Discovery located official legacy documentation but not a verified current bulk numeric endpoint.
Contributed state-survey records may overlap upstream releases.

us-wqp-sacramento-river-arsenic.title: USGS Sacramento River at Freeport dissolved arsenic via Water Quality Portal
us-wqp-sacramento-river-arsenic.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey California Water Science Center via the Water Quality Portal

coverage.notes: One USGS stream station with 189 dissolved-As observations from 2010-2023; method-rich independent freshwater validation, not national coverage.

license.notes: The pinned records are USGS/NWIS data. Retain USGS, WQP, station, query, access time and result identifiers.

limitations: The exact query repeated As, Cu, Ni and Zn parameters, but the response contained only dissolved arsenic; unreturned elements are not claimed.
This is one station and cannot fill the geographic coverage gap of a national or global river network.
Fifty-seven results are preliminary and ten are field-replicate QC samples; both statuses remain explicit.
The one Not Detected result is left-censored at its reported limit and is not converted to zero.
Portal aggregation is not independent evidence from the upstream USGS/NWIS provider.

us-water-quality-portal.title: Water Quality Portal
us-water-quality-portal.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and National Water Quality Monitoring Council

coverage.notes: Programmatic access to WQX and NWIS water-quality records from many organizations and sample media.

license.notes: Federal records may be public domain, but WQX contains many contributor organizations; retain provider and dataset terms per record.

limitations: Portal aggregation is not an independent source from NWIS or WQX providers.
Characteristic names, sample fractions, detection limits, qualifiers and organization methods are highly heterogeneous.

soils4africa.title: Soils4Africa soil point data

coverage.notes: Harmonised 2022-2024 point observations and laboratory chemical properties across sampled African agricultural land.

license.notes: CC BY 4.0 use is accompanied by anti-identification and reporting/aggregation conditions that must be implemented before production.

limitations: The licence warns that points are not representative of local or field conditions.
The exact elemental analyte inventory and privacy-safe output policy require audit before routing.

bgs-gbase.title: Geochemical Baseline Survey of the Environment (G-BASE)

coverage.notes: Long-running baseline survey of soil, stream sediment, stream water and panned concentrates across the UK.

license.notes: Derived grids are OGL; underpinning survey point observations require a separate BGS licence and are not open-only production data.

limitations: Open interpolated grids are derived products and cannot substitute for source point observations.
Point data cannot enter the open-only production route without a compatible explicit licence.

brazil-sgb-geochemistry.title: GeoSGB integrated geochemical samples

coverage.notes: National geochemical sample service and project releases spanning several sample media and survey periods.

license.notes: Open access is stated for repository items, but reuse/redistribution terms for the integrated service need verification.

limitations: Integrated points and project ZIP releases may duplicate each other.
Field definitions, sample-medium codes, analytical methods and licence need source-level verification.

nz-petlab.title: Petlab: New Zealand national rock, mineral and geoanalytical database

coverage.notes: National curated sample and analytical database with contributed university collections and selected offshore/global material.

license.notes: A free account is required for export; download and redistribution terms need review.

limitations: Dynamic database version and export inventory must be recorded for reproducibility.
Published, thesis and collection data require original-reference retention and duplicate review.

earthchem-library.title: EarthChem Library

coverage.notes: Curated DOI repository for contributed Earth and planetary science datasets; each deposited dataset has its own scope and licence.

license.notes: Depositors choose among CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA and non-commercial Creative Commons licences; filter at dataset level.

limitations: Repository inclusion is not uniform geochemical coverage or method comparability.
Each DOI dataset must pass its own licence, schema, file-identity, row-count, citation and duplicate checks before use.

geotraces-idp2025.title: GEOTRACES Intermediate Data Product 2025
geotraces-idp2025.publisher: GEOTRACES International Project Office and NERC EDS British Oceanographic Data Centre

coverage.notes: The full IDP2025 product reports 123 cruises and 4,097 stations across all packages. The verified discrete-seawater collection exposes 4,094 stations and 82 cruise labels; the Cu/Ni/Zn OR-filtered export contains target-bearing samples from 46 cruises and 1,550 cruise-station pairs.

license.notes: Fair Use Agreement requires IDP and original data-contributor citations.

limitations: Cruise-track ocean sampling is not uniform global surface-water coverage.
Dissolved, particulate and other fractions plus quality flags and contributor citations must remain distinct.
The official IDP2025 seawater parameter inventory contains dissolved Cu, Ni and Zn but no arsenic variable; another water source is required for As.
The frozen webODV export preserves nmol/kg. It must not be mixed with ug/L without an explicit element-specific atomic-mass and seawater-density conversion.
SeaDataNet flags 3 and 4 identify probably-bad and bad values; they remain traceable raw records but are excluded from the demonstration slice.
The adapter and 30-row review sheet are prepared, but named human review is still incomplete.

glorich.title: GLORICH Global River Chemistry Database
glorich.publisher: PANGAEA Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Science

coverage.notes: Compilation of more than 1.27 million samples from more than 18,000 river sampling locations, focused on major compounds, nutrients and carbon.

license.notes: Non-commercial restriction excludes this dataset from the current open-only production route.

limitations: Compilation inherits heterogeneous source methods and possible overlap with national/international portals.
Focus is major compounds and nutrients rather than comprehensive trace-element coverage.

eea-waterbase.title: Waterbase water quality data

coverage.notes: European reporting database for rivers, lakes, groundwater, transitional, coastal and marine waters, including chemical-quality observations.

license.notes: EEA permits commercial and non-commercial reuse with attribution, subject to dataset-specific third-party notices; exact machine-readable licence needs pinning.

limitations: National reporting coverage, determinands and methods vary by country and year.
Water, sediment and biota results must be separated by matrix and fraction.

noaa-ncei-marine-geology.title: NCEI Marine Geology Data Archive and IMLGS
noaa-ncei-marine-geology.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

coverage.notes: Long-term heterogeneous archive of marine and lacustrine rock and sediment analyses, descriptions, images and sample metadata from many contributing programs.

license.notes: NOAA requests citation of the original source and DOI where provided; each archived numerical dataset must retain its own source and reuse terms.

limitations: IMLGS is primarily a sample inventory and cannot be treated as a table of geochemical measurements.
Archive files are heterogeneous and must be accepted, versioned and cited at the original dataset level.

pangaea-north-africa-soil.title: Chemical compositions of deflatable soil fractions from North Africa
pangaea-north-africa-soil.publisher: PANGAEA Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Science

coverage.notes: Forty-three discrete sample rows spanning publisher coordinates -13.26 to 32.50 degrees longitude and 15.67 to 33.83 degrees latitude; not a continuous regional grid.

license.notes: Dataset-level CC BY 4.0 permits research use with attribution to the named authors, DOI and repository.

limitations: The table contains 43 discrete samples and cannot be described as uniform North African coverage.
The analysed material is the less-than-20-micrometre fine silt-clay fraction after HF-HNO3 digestion, so values are not automatically comparable with bulk-soil or partial-extraction surveys.
Publisher location strings include border descriptions; country must not be inferred solely from coordinates.
The source reports international reference-material agreement within plus or minus 10 percent, but no row-level detection limits are present in Table S5.

pangaea-repository.title: PANGAEA Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Science
pangaea-repository.publisher: Alfred Wegener Institute and MARUM, University of Bremen

coverage.notes: Open-access repository for georeferenced observational and experimental Earth-system datasets, including many publication-linked geochemical datasets.

license.notes: The licence is stated on each dataset; recent defaults do not replace dataset-level checks for historical, moratorium or community-specific records.

limitations: Repository search results are not one harmonised geochemical dataset.
Every DOI must pass separate media, method, licence, file-identity, schema, row-count, citation and duplicate checks.

iodp-data-systems.title: IODP, ODP and DSDP expedition data systems
iodp-data-systems.publisher: International Ocean Discovery Program and its Science Operators

coverage.notes: Expedition data include core and borehole rock or sediment measurements plus chemistry such as interstitial-water observations; coverage follows scientific drilling sites.

license.notes: Data access, moratorium status, citations and policies vary by program, science operator, expedition and derived publication.

limitations: Legacy and current data are fragmented across multiple operator systems and schemas.
Pore-water, solid-core and downhole records must remain separate and retain expedition, hole, depth and method context.

emodnet-chemistry.title: EMODnet Chemistry
emodnet-chemistry.publisher: European Marine Observation and Data Network Chemistry partnership

coverage.notes: Marine water and sediment chemistry from European data centres, with discovery records and regularly compiled harmonised data products.

license.notes: CDI records include both freely downloadable and restricted data; harmonised ERDDAP collections are compiled from unrestricted measurements but still require originator lineage.

limitations: The portal and derived collections can repeat data available from national providers, SeaDataNet or EEA systems.
Water, sediment and biota plus dissolved, particulate and total fractions must be separated before use.

jamstec-darwin.title: JAMSTEC DARWIN cruise data and sample information system
jamstec-darwin.publisher: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

coverage.notes: Cruise, dive and sample discovery for JAMSTEC research vessels and submersibles, including rock and sediment-core sample catalogues.

license.notes: Cruise policy, moratorium, citation and data-quality class vary by record; commercial use requires advance application.

limitations: The current official pages verify sample and observation discovery, not a uniform numerical geochemistry endpoint.
Legacy GANSEKI references are not counted as a separate active source until their current data lineage is resolved.
Commercial use requires advance application, so DARWIN remains outside the open-only automatic route.

ireland-tellus.title: Geological Survey Ireland Tellus geochemistry data

coverage.notes: Tellus releases include multi-element shallow and deeper soil, stream-sediment and stream-water geochemistry with methods and release documentation.

license.notes: The official open-data policy and exact licence notice on each downloadable release must be pinned together.

limitations: Tellus releases and legacy national or regional surveys must be versioned and deduplicated separately.
The main GSI website was temporarily offline during this review, so exact files and licence notices need a fresh endpoint check before admission.

sweden-sgu-geochemical-atlas.title: Geochemical Atlas of Sweden data

coverage.notes: Downloadable national till geochemistry for the atlas; associated tables document methods, detection limits and comparisons with agricultural and grazing-land soil.

license.notes: The official data endpoint is public, but an exact reuse licence must be pinned before production.

limitations: The verified raw download is till data; summary tables for soil comparisons are not equivalent to raw soil observations.
Aqua-regia extraction, grain-size fraction, detection limits and sample medium must remain explicit.

finland-gtk-geochemistry.title: GTK national rock and regional geochemistry services

coverage.notes: National rock-geochemistry product plus till and stream-sediment layers exposed through GTK Hakku and ArcGIS services.

license.notes: The listed national rock product is free with an open licence, while other GTK products and detailed assay services may have separate terms or fees.

limitations: Rock, regional till, detailed till and stream-sediment layers are separate surveys and cannot share one method assumption.
Each selected layer or download must pin its licence, schema, sample count, method and service version.

norway-ngu-lito.title: LITO geochemical mapping of Norwegian bedrock

coverage.notes: Systematic national bedrock geochemistry sampled on an approximately 9 by 9 kilometre grid, with major, trace and rare-earth element methods.

license.notes: The spreadsheet is publicly downloadable, but its exact reuse licence and citation contract need to be pinned.

limitations: The June 2026 dataset is explicitly under development and has not completed final rock-name and batch-adjustment quality control.
A pinned version label is not sufficient for admission until file identity, byte count, licence, schema, row counts and QC flags are verified.

norway-marchem.title: MarChem marine chemistry database for Norwegian waters
norway-marchem.publisher: Institute of Marine Research and Geological Survey of Norway

coverage.notes: Contaminants and environmental characteristics measured in marine sediments from MAREANO and other Norwegian mapping and monitoring programs.

license.notes: The service states CC BY 4.0 and Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data; dataset landing-page citations and acknowledgements still apply.

limitations: The database contains natural elements and anthropogenic contaminants; target-analyte scope must be selected explicitly.

The verified public API export is dynamic and timestamped; the selected inorganic response is fixed by request, observation time, member inventory, byte counts and scientific row statistics but has no matching immutable DOI.
The As, Cu, Ni and Zn measurements are reported on a dry-weight basis after partial nitric-acid digestion and must not be represented as total content.
Batch metadata mix accredited and not-accredited analyses, and the export can repeat a sample across parameter groups; both facts must survive record-level mapping.

mexico-sgm-geochemical-cartography.title: Cartografía geoquímica de México, escala 1:250,000

coverage.notes: National 1:250,000 geochemical cartography generated from active stream-sediment analyses collected in the 1995–2005 mapping program; the published layer is an interpreted map product, not yet verified as a row-level measurement table.

license.notes: The federal open-data catalogue labels the dataset CC BY 4.0, while GeoInfoMex also reserves copyright and prohibits for-profit reproduction without prior permission. Research access is plausible, but the exact file-level notice and attribution contract must be preserved and reconciled.

limitations: The verified public product is described as an interpretation layer derived from active stream-sediment analyses; raw sample values, methods and detection limits are not yet confirmed.
The federal catalogue and GeoInfoMex notices are not yet reconciled at the downloaded-file level.
Map sheets using different geodetic reference frames can contain gaps or overlaps.

canada-bc-rgs.title: British Columbia Regional Geochemical Survey database

coverage.notes: Province-wide compilation of stream and lake sediment, drainage-water, heavy-mineral-concentrate and related survey media; the 2020 release reports 65,000 samples and about five million determinations from 116 original sources.

license.notes: The release is publicly downloadable through the provincial site; the exact Open Government Licence notice and any third-party conditions from the 116 original sources must be bound to the selected files before use.

limitations: The compilation integrates 116 original releases, so independence and duplicate handling must follow the original survey and sample identifiers.
Eighteen analytical methods and laboratories cannot be combined without record-level method mapping.
Vegetation and moss-mat observations fall outside the current four-media production contract and require separate medium terms.

alaska-dggs-webgeochem.title: Alaska Geochemistry Database (WebGeochem)
alaska-dggs-webgeochem.publisher: Alaska Division of Geological & Geophysical Surveys

coverage.notes: Ongoing Alaska database combining DGGS, USGS, BLM and former U.S. Bureau of Mines records, including modern laboratory spreadsheets and legacy reports.

license.notes: Recent DGGS raw-data releases state an open end-user licence, while the integrated database also contains federal and legacy sources. Acceptance must occur per publication or upstream contributor.

limitations: The database mixes scanned legacy reports, federal databases and direct laboratory imports; original publication and analytical lineage must remain record-level facts.
The dynamic all-record export is not itself an immutable version; prefer pinned DGGS publication packages for the first adapter.
Coordinate datums and method packages vary between releases.

chile-sernageomin-geochemistry.title: Programa de Cartografía Geoquímica de Chile
chile-sernageomin-geochemistry.publisher: Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería de Chile

coverage.notes: Regional drainage-sediment mapping program; an official 2025 report states more than 10,000 samples over more than 230,000 square kilometres, with up to 66 elements per sample.

license.notes: Public viewers and product pages are available, but access price, research-use terms, attribution and downloadable-file rights must be checked for each map-sheet database.

limitations: Coverage is a set of regional sheets and river-basin products, not a continuous national grid.
The program total cannot substitute for per-sheet file, schema, method, detection-limit and licence verification.
Viewer layers and downloadable Excel products may be alternate representations of the same samples and must be deduplicated.

argentina-segemar-geochemistry.title: SIGAM multielement geochemical sample data

coverage.notes: SIGAM exposes multielement chemistry and locations for stream-sediment and soil samples; SEGEMAR annual reports describe more than 40,000 stream-sediment records.

license.notes: The service identifies itself as an open geospatial data catalogue, but the exact research-use, download and attribution notice must be captured from each selected metadata record.

limitations: The stated total spans historical archive samples and newer SEGEMAR sampling; date, method and coordinate uncertainty differ by project.
The 54-element map description is a regional cartographic product and does not prove identical analyte coverage for every record.
Repository PDFs, SIGAM layers and sheet products can repeat the same survey samples.

india-gsi-ngcm.title: Geological Survey of India National Geochemical Mapping Programme

coverage.notes: National program based primarily on stream-sediment sampling in 2 by 2 kilometre cells, with official program documents describing analysis for 66 elements and a target 1:50,000 seamless map.

license.notes: The official atlas currently exposes no downloadable records and the located numerical distribution route is event/login specific; research-use terms and a durable public endpoint remain unresolved.

limitations: The official atlas returned zero records during this review, so the program cannot yet supply an automated production route.
Hackathon files cover selected toposheets and are not evidence of a stable national bulk release.
Program descriptions must not be used to infer that all planned cells, elements or metadata are publicly available.

japan-gsj-geochemical-map.title: Geochemical Map of Japan

coverage.notes: This implemented dataset contains 3,024 national river-sediment sample rows. Marine sediment, later regional additions and surface soil remain separate candidate products.

license.notes: GSJ states that research products published on its website follow Japan Government Standard Terms of Use 2.0 and may be reused with attribution; third-party content remains excluded.

limitations: The implemented pair contains river sediment only; marine sediment, regional supplements and later surface-soil products remain separate.
The 3,024 samples follow river catchments and do not form a uniform national grid.
Coordinates are JGD2000 and require explicit transformation before WGS84 output.
Sample ID 78013 occurs twice in each file and must be joined by occurrence order.
Hg is ppb while registered As, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn values are ppm.
The CSV pair has no row-level method, detection-limit or QC fields; method evidence must be resolved from project publications.

afsis-phase-i-wet-chemistry.title: AfSIS Phase I archived soil samples: wet chemistry data

coverage.notes: The release contains 2,002 topsoil and subsoil samples from 51 LDSF sentinel sites. It is broad multi-country evidence, not a continuous or statistically uniform African grid.

license.notes: Version 2.0 terms specify CC BY 4.0; retain dataset and article citations.

limitations: The LDSF field design and available archived samples are not uniform national or continental coverage.
Aqua-regia results are quasi-total and must remain separate from total or differently extracted soil values.
One hundred twenty-six samples have no coordinates and cannot enter coordinate-dependent mapping without additional evidence.
The source contains negative numeric instrument results and many positive values below source-wide DL or QL; these remain explicit quality flags.
Raw country labels SAfrica and Zimbambwe require a separate normalization field while retaining the publisher strings.
The registered files and related article do not state the coordinate reference system, so the adapter does not assert EPSG:4326.
The variable workbook describes As.75 as Arsenic-78 and reports 2009-2013 sampling, while the related paper reports 2009-2012; these metadata conflicts require source-level review.

tpdc-china-mountain-soil.title: Multi-element dataset of soil profiles across climatic zones in China's mountains
tpdc-china-mountain-soil.publisher: National Tibetan Plateau / Third Pole Environment Data Center

coverage.notes: The release contains 1,314 O-, A- and C-horizon samples from 166 sites in 30 mountain ecosystems and five climate zones. It is a targeted mountain survey, not a spatially continuous or nationally representative China soil grid.

license.notes: The dataset metadata records licence code 1, which the TPDC interface maps to CC BY 4.0. Retain the dataset DOI, authors and TPDC attribution.

limitations: The survey covers 30 mountain ecosystems and cannot be described as uniform nationwide China coverage.
The release contains Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn among the project targets but does not contain As or Hg.
O, A and C horizons are scientifically distinct and must remain separate sample types and comparison groups.
The source records GPS coordinates but the registered metadata and data files do not declare a coordinate reference system; no EPSG code may be inferred.
Three site labels (SN5, SN6 and SN7) have more than one published coordinate pair and must retain sample-level coordinates rather than a forced site centroid.

The separate bulk-density workbook can fill 58 missing main-table rows, but six non-missing bulk-density values and five coordinates conflict with the main workbook; supplemental values must never overwrite published main-table values silently.

The main workbook has no row-level detection-limit, qualifier or method fields. Dataset-level preparation, digestion, ICP-AES/ICP-MS and QC evidence comes from the linked article and must carry dataset or publication scope.

australia-ngsa-mercury.title: National Geochemical Survey of Australia: Mercury Concentrations Dataset

coverage.notes: 2,396 TOS/BOS records at 1,247 sites across seven states and territories; national catchment survey rather than a regular grid.

license.notes: The publisher file states CC BY 4.0 Australia; retain dataset DOI and Geoscience Australia attribution.

limitations: Only Hg is present in this product; it does not supply the other target elements.
Top and bottom outlet sediment are separate horizons and cannot be pooled without an explicit comparison decision.
The reported 0.01 ng Hg limit is a mass LOD, not a concentration-row threshold.
Duplicate codes identify QA/QC structure and do not create independent spatial sites.
Catchment sampling is nationally broad but spatially discrete and uneven.

japan-gsj-marine-sediment.title: Geochemical Map of Sea and Land of Japan: marine sediment concentrations

coverage.notes: 4,905 marine sediment samples from 37 cruises and 37 named regions; separate from the implemented national river-sediment product.

license.notes: GSJ website research products follow Japan Government Standard Terms of Use 2.0 with attribution; third-party material remains excluded.

limitations: Marine and river sediment remain separate source products and sample types.
Hg uses ppb while the other target fields use ppm.
The concentration CSV has no row-level method, detection-limit or QC fields.
Ten negative Hg values are preserved as source results and are not ordinary positive concentrations.
Cruise sampling tracks do not constitute continuous coverage of Japanese seas.

pangaea-arabian-sea-sediment.title: Geochemistry of modern sediments and the glacial Arabian Sea
pangaea-arabian-sea-sediment.publisher: PANGAEA Data Publisher for Earth & Environmental Science

coverage.notes: Twenty-seven rows from 26 named events between 10.03-19.52 N and 57.36-68.37 E; a method-linked long-tail dataset rather than a regional grid.

license.notes: PANGAEA records CC BY 4.0; retain dataset and bundled-publication citations.

limitations: Twenty-seven source rows are not continuous Arabian Sea coverage.
The source method label is generic and does not specify an instrument or digestion.
One sample label has two source rows and must retain row identity.
Core depth and sea-floor elevation are distinct quantities and must not be interchanged.
This publication-linked dataset may overlap later aggregations and must be deduplicated by event, sample and DOI lineage.

south-africa-cgs-geochemistry.title: Council for Geoscience geochemistry map services

coverage.notes: National portal exposes multiple map-sheet geochemistry layers; a verified Alexander Bay point layer contains stream-sediment or fallback surface-soil samples with As, Cu, Ni, Zn and other elemental fields.

license.notes: CGS retains copyright and intellectual-property rights in the verified layer. The project may query it for research discovery, but adapter use must capture the complete product licence and any use restrictions before normal routing.

limitations: The portal is a collection of map-sheet products, not one proven continuous national measurement table.
The verified layer mixes preferred stream sediment with fallback surface soil; record-level medium identification is required.
Method, unit, detection-limit, version and full licence metadata have not yet been reconciled for the representative layer.
